receipts.first_text_witness: Have you ever stared at your retirement account options feeling like you're trying to decode ancient hieroglyphics written by caffeinated financial adviserss? You're not alone. When most people open up their 401k menu for the first time, they're greeted with a bewildering array of fund names that sound like they were generated by throwing alphabet soup at a wall. large cap growth, midcap value, international emerging markets, target date funds, and somewhere in that maze of confusion sits something called the S&P 500 index fund. Now, if you're like most people, you've probably heard the term S&P 500 thrown around
receipts.last_text_witness: PhD to understand. It's simply a way to own pieces of America's most successful companies without having to research each one individually or pay someone in an expensive suit to pretend they can predict the future. Whether you choose the basic S&P 500 index fund or opt for something with a bit more growth potential is entirely up to your risk tolerance and timeline. Just remember, the best investment strategy is the one you'll actually stick with for decades, not the one that sounds the most impressive at dinner parties.

primary_source_receipts.finding: 89.50% of U.S. large-cap funds underperformed S&P 500 over 15 years; rounded 90% is supported for this specified window. One-year rate was 65.24%.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Not all managers every year; historical fund survival/methodology and benchmark costs matter. Transcript does not name end date.

primary_source_receipts.finding: Selected index fund annual gain 8.5%; five selected funds-of-funds reported 2.0/3.6/6.5/0.3/2.4%. Protégé chose funds-of-funds investing in 200+ hedge funds.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Selected historical bet; D liquidated; not a universal hedge-fund comparison.
primary_source_receipts.locator: The Bet; PDF pp10–11, printed pp11–12

primary_source_receipts.finding: Asset-weighted active equity mutual fund expense ratio 0.64%, index equity 0.05%; all equity 0.40%; all-equity simple average 1.10%.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Population averages differ; excludes variable-annuity funds. A particular active fund can charge 1–2%, but that is not the asset-weighted typical experience.

primary_source_receipts.finding: VOO listed expense ratio 0.03%, equivalent to $3 per $10K or $150 per $500K at constant balance.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Example product only; fees/spreads can vary; not evidence of all index fund charges.

primary_source_receipts.finding: IRA limit $7K; extra $1K catch-up applies age 50+. Roth phaseouts for 2025 are $150K–165K single and $236K–246K joint.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Eligibility and compensation matter; no future contribution limits assumed.

primary_source_receipts.finding: Roth contributions not deductible; qualified withdrawals tax-free; combined IRA limit and modified-AGI rules apply.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Live page, not a captured 2025 edition; historical limit separately anchored to IRS_2025.
primary_source_receipts.locator: Roth IRAs, contribution and modified-AGI sections

primary_source_receipts.finding: Funds track rather than directly constitute an investable index; full or sampled replication; costs/tracking error and market risks persist. Lower fees can improve net results with identical holdings.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: General education, not evidence of guaranteed returns or all advisors motives.
primary_source_receipts.locator: Index Funds: definition, holdings, costs and risks

primary_source_receipts.finding: U.S. large-cap index uses float-adjusted capitalization and committee governance. New additions generally require positive latest quarter and sum of four quarters; IPO seasoning normally 12 months; migration/spinoff exceptions exist.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Current methodology cannot certify exact Dec2025 thresholds/rules; precise historical version not retrieved. Membership is not a guarantee of business quality or future gains.
primary_source_receipts.locator: Eligibility financial viability/IPO rules pp9–10; weighting and governance

primary_source_receipts.finding: S&P reports top ten companies represented almost 40% of index by mid2025.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Weight share is not fixed share of realized performance. Not an exact upload-date constituent table; Johnson & Johnson top-ten implication unverified.

primary_source_receipts.finding: Index describes 500 leading U.S. companies covering about 80% of available capitalization; launch date March 4, 1957. Prelaunch data described as hypothetical back-tested.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: No exact 90-year CAGR independently reconstructed; price/total return and averaging choice unspecified in video. Index is not GDP or all world markets.

primary_source_receipts.finding: ETF ownership is a share in a fund; implementation, pricing and expenses require review.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Does not establish no trading/research/management work or guaranteed investor suitability.

calculation_receipts.assumptions_and_limits: Frozen rounded ages; same channel/format/snapshot; >=7 days; peer ages .5–2x; sort age distance then ID. Lifetime association, not current velocity or cause.
Simple constant-balance illustration; actual fees accrue on changing NAV. VOO is an example, not a transcript-named product. $3 pertains to $10K, not $500K.

End-month contributions, fixed positive rates, no taxes/fees. 7%/12 compounds to >7% effective annual. If 7% is real, $1K must be constant purchasing power to interpret FV as real; fixed nominal deposits are different.

Constant contributions and nominal effective annual 10%; hypothetical, not forecast or future legal limit. $227K resembles $6.5K*35=$227.5K, inconsistent with stated $7–8K. $1.4M does not follow either stated input under these standard timings.
Analyst illustration, no contributions; subtracting fee from return is simplified annual convention. Hundreds of thousands is balance/horizon/return dependent, not automatic.
Conditional on same cash contribution and execution; 50% decline needs 100% recovery. More shares does not guarantee higher terminal wealth or ability to keep contributing.

Berkshire 2017 letter printed p12; D operated nine years and was liquidated. Mean of reported CAGRs is not a pooled ten-year portfolio CAGR; population is five selected funds-of-funds, not all hedge funds.
